metrics.howToMeasure: Watershed wetland (%), woody plus herbaceous, both classes required; wetlands store surface water and attenuate flow peaks. EASI scores Surface water storage on the same sum (method watershed-wetland-extent).
metrics.methodContext: Percent of the watershed in woody plus herbaceous wetland (NLCD 2019). DEEP reads it from EPA StreamCat for the reach. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 82), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.
Scored on a reference pool whose transfer to this ecoregion was not confirmed by the recovery test (class agreement 0.57 of evaluation regions; two thirds required); confidence capped at 39.

referenceSupport.screen: least-disturbed-regional-v1 (relaxed tier, watershed agriculture at most 25 percent, the 25 percent floor)
referenceSupport.transferNote: 22 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) of this ecoregion. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.57 of 7 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.01, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

metrics.howToMeasure: Road density (km/sq km) is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good <1 km/km², Fair 1-<3 km/km², Poor ≥3 km/km².
metrics.methodContext: Road length per square kilometer of watershed. DEEP computes it for the delineated watershed. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: EASI fixed criteria, Road-density proxy for concentrated inflow pressure

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Road-density proxy for concentrated inflow pressure

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
USDA Forest Service 2011, Watershed Condition Classification Technical Guide (FS-978)

limitations: Road density does not count actual outfalls or establish whether runoff is treated.
The 1 km/km² breakpoint is a screening judgment.

USFS watershed-condition guidance classes road density more strictly (good under 1, impaired over 2.4 miles per square mile, about 0.62 and 1.49 km/km²), derived from salmonid watersheds. EASI keeps the NRSA-anchored national screen and discloses the stricter alternative.

metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 82), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.
metrics.methodContext: Base flow index of the watershed, the percent of streamflow that comes from base flow (USGS base flow index grid). DEEP reads it from EPA StreamCat for the reach. Nothing is measured in the field.

metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 82), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Residual pool depth per 100 m; deeper residual pools generally better habitat.
metrics.methodContext: Measure the thalweg depth at 10 or 15 evenly spaced stations between each pair of transects (100 or 150 along the reach). The value is the mean residual pool depth in centimeters, computed from that depth profile and the reach slope with the NRSA physical habitat calculations.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 82), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 8.1 (Mixed Wood Plains) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 44 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 8.1 (Mixed Wood Plains), 21 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, surficial lithology. The national scale analysis supports this metric at Level III, finer than the level borrowed from, so the transfer risk is moderate and the expectation may not represent local conditions.

metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 82), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Log relative bed stability; departure from the reference core in EITHER direction departs from reference (negative excess fines, positive an armored, sediment-starved bed, the classic below-impoundment failure). The pilot's rising direction scored armored beds 1.0 and left Sediment continuity blind to its textbook failure mode. Two-sided form is an owner decision at the adversarial review gate, 2026-08-21.
metrics.methodContext: Computed, not read in the field. It is the base 10 logarithm of the ratio of the geometric mean particle diameter to the largest diameter the bankfull flow can move, from the particle count, reach slope, bankfull depth, wood tally and residual pools, with the NRSA physical habitat calculations.

metrics.sourceCitation: EASI fixed criteria, Nearby dam-proximity proxy
metrics.howToMeasure: Mapped dams within one mile is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good 0 mapped dams, Fair 1 mapped dam, Poor ≥2 mapped dams.
metrics.methodContext: Number of dams in the USACE National Inventory of Dams within one mile of the site. DEEP counts them. Note in the field any barrier the inventory does not show.

curve.layerName: EASI fixed criteria, Nearby dam-proximity proxy

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

citations.text: USACE National Inventory of Dams

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.
metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 5 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 5 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 12 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 4 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 4 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 12 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: High missingness. 45% of the 22 comparable reference stations of this ecoregion's own reference pool have no value for this metric (12 carry one), above the 40% limit of rule DATA-03, so the metric is withheld at the build. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 23), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from NARS-9 region ecoregion WMT because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 163 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region WMT, 14 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.63 of 19 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.08, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 11 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 5 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 6 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 1 carries the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 4 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 5 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 9 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. The Level II pool (13.1): The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. The Level I pool (13): The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.40 over 101 reference and 99 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.
metrics.methodContext: Base flow index of the watershed, the percent of streamflow that comes from base flow (USGS base flow index grid). DEEP reads it from EPA StreamCat for the reach. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 22), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 10.1 (Cold Deserts) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 54 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 10.1 (Cold Deserts), 6 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

metrics.howToMeasure: Impervious surface (%) is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good <10%, Fair 10-25%, Poor >25%.
metrics.methodContext: Percent of the watershed in impervious surface. DEEP computes it for the delineated watershed. Nothing is measured in the field.

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness
Allan 2004, Landscapes and riverscapes: the influence of land use on stream ecosystems
Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams
King et al. 2011, Stream community thresholds at exceptionally low levels of catchment urbanization

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.
Agricultural bands are national screening tiers, not ecological criteria.
A result computed from one input is labeled partial.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 19 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 3 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 13 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 1 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (10.1): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.33 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level I pool (10): The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. The NARS-9 pool (XER): The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 18 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.31 over 30 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 32 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the donor pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

rungsTried.why: 18 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.31 over 30 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 32 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the donor pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built.
The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric.

Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 1 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 2 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (10.1): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.22 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level I pool (10): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.37 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The NARS-9 pool (XER): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.22 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 20 matched national donors, but the donor pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.79 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. 139 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 37), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 8.4 (Ozark/Ouachita-Appalachian Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 61 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 37.8 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region SAP, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 8.4 (Ozark/Ouachita-Appalachian Forests), 4 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. metrics.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 19 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 6 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 15 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 2 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 4 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (8.4): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.29 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.33 over 50 reference and 1116 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (SAP): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.35 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 20 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.43 over 36 reference and 2032 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 14 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the donor pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.41 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. Modeled reference: The low-disturbance training streams cover the natural setting of 0% of this ecoregion's streams, less than the 7% of the weakest region the model was validated in, so the prediction would extrapolate past where it was tested. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include no regional criterion for turbidity. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

The low-disturbance training streams cover the natural setting of 0% of this ecoregion's streams, less than the 7% of the weakest region the model was validated in, so the prediction would extrapolate past where it was tested.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (8.5): 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level I pool (8): 9 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The NARS-9 pool (CPL): 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 17 matched national donors, but the donor pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.25 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. 1 national donors inside the comparability envelope, below the floor of 10. Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
metrics.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 23 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 4 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 3 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.20 over 20 reference and 10 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). This ecoregion under the regional screen: The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.20 over 21 reference and 10 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level II pool (8.4): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.35 over 53 reference and 191 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.36 over 99 reference and 1014 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (SAP): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.36 over 76 reference and 313 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 8.4 (Ozark/Ouachita-Appalachian Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 34 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 37.8 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region SAP, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 8.4 (Ozark/Ouachita-Appalachian Forests), 4 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.67 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.16, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 41), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 6.2 (Western Cordillera) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 105 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 6.2 (Western Cordillera), 13 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.67 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.16, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 8 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 14 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 2 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 9 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 5 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 5 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (6.2): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (6): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 37 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 103 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 23 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 2 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 2 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 3 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. The Level II pool (6.2): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (6): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 53 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.26 over 105 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 117 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 69), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: The reference expectation likely varies with ElevationClass (cross-validated improvement 17%, resample recurrence 82%); the curve is unstratified pending a larger reference pool, so sites at either end of that gradient may read as departures that are natural.
Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 8.4 (Ozark/Ouachita-Appalachian Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 56 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 37.8 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region SAP, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 8.4 (Ozark/Ouachita-Appalachian Forests), 5 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 18 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 6 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 12 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 2 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (8.4): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.35 over 50 reference and 191 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.38 over 97 reference and 1014 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (SAP): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.41 over 62 reference and 313 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 48 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.39 over 117 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 48 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.28 over 48 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from NARS-9 region ecoregion XER because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 66 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region XER, 18 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, air temperature. Every station drains to this ecoregion's faunal province. The national scale analysis supports this metric at Level II, finer than the level borrowed from, so the transfer risk is moderate and the expectation may not represent local conditions.

Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness

Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 16 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 1 curve is fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 4 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 4 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 2 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 2 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 1.00 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 1.00 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level II pool (10.1): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (10): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (XER): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 70 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.25 over 129 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 148 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.24 over 148 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

metrics.howToMeasure: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). metrics.methodContext: Base flow index of the watershed, the percent of streamflow that comes from base flow (USGS base flow index grid). DEEP reads it from EPA StreamCat for the reach. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 6), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from NARS-9 region ecoregion XER because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 36 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region XER, 5 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.26 of 19 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.11, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

metrics.howToMeasure: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 7), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from NARS-9 region ecoregion XER because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 46 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region XER, 2 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.26 of 19 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.11, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

metrics.transferNote: 17 least-disturbed stations from the national pool, the three nearest to each of this ecoregion's streams on the natural setting that governs this metric family, none inside this ecoregion. referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 13 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 6 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 2 carry the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 17 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness
Allan 2004, Landscapes and riverscapes: the influence of land use on stream ecosystems
Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams
King et al. 2011, Stream community thresholds at exceptionally low levels of catchment urbanization

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.

The test found class agreement 0.56 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.00, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness
Allan 2004, Landscapes and riverscapes: the influence of land use on stream ecosystems
Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams
King et al. 2011, Stream community thresholds at exceptionally low levels of catchment urbanization

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.
Agricultural bands are national screening tiers, not ecological criteria.
A result computed from one input is labeled partial.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 23 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 4 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 18 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (8.2): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (TPL): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 46 matched national donors, but the donor pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.31 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. 90 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: A modeled specification for this metric passed the recovery test and waits for the owner's approval, so it is not used yet. curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 27), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: The reference expectation likely varies with ElevationClass (cross-validated improvement 32%, resample recurrence 98%); the curve is unstratified pending a larger reference pool, so sites at either end of that gradient may read as departures that are natural.
Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 9.4 (South Central Semi-Arid Prairies) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 45 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 9.4 (South Central Semi-Arid Prairies), 5 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 16 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 6 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 10 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Measurement-precision floor. The Functioning core of this two-sided curve spans 0.395 Std. Units (7.93 to 8.32 Std. Units at n = 40), narrower than 0.4 Std. Units, so band assignments inside it would present measurement noise as condition classes and the metric is withheld at the build under rule CURVE-09. citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document

Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. metrics.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 13 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 8 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 14 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 2 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 4 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (10.2): 4 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level I pool (10): 7 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The NARS-9 pool (XER): 7 usable stations, below the floor of 10. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 7 matched national donors, below the floor of 10. 21 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.34 over 21 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

metrics.howToMeasure: Impervious surface (%) is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good <10%, Fair 10-25%, Poor >25%.

criteriaSource.title: Catchment hydrology (land-cover pressure)

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness
Allan 2004, Landscapes and riverscapes: the influence of land use on stream ecosystems
Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams
King et al. 2011, Stream community thresholds at exceptionally low levels of catchment urbanization

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.
Agricultural bands are national screening tiers, not ecological criteria.
A result computed from one input is labeled partial.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

referenceSupport.screen: least-disturbed-regional-v1 (relaxed tier, watershed agriculture at most 25 percent, the 25 percent floor)
referenceSupport.transferNote: 38 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) of this ecoregion. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.57 of 7 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.14, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness
Allan 2004, Landscapes and riverscapes: the influence of land use on stream ecosystems
Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.
Agricultural bands are national screening tiers, not ecological criteria.
A result computed from one input is labeled partial.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 13 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 5 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 2 carry the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 13 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 5 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 7 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (10.1): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (10): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (XER): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 25 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.25 over 78 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 39 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.
