curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 10.1 (Cold Deserts) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 60 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 10.1 (Cold Deserts), 13 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.67 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.16, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 7 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 2 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 13 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 3 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 4 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 21 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 5 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 13 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 1 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (8.1): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.45 over 17 reference and 331 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.37 over 20 reference and 1014 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (UMW): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.32 over 24 reference and 190 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 39 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.44 over 204 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 26 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.40 over 26 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. metrics.howToMeasure: Mapped dams within one mile is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good 0 mapped dams, Fair 1 mapped dam, Poor ≥2 mapped dams.
metrics.methodContext: Number of dams in the USACE National Inventory of Dams within one mile of the site. DEEP counts them. Note in the field any barrier the inventory does not show.

curve.layerName: EASI fixed criteria, Nearby dam-proximity proxy

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

citations.text: USACE National Inventory of Dams

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.
metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 19 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 5 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 12 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 6 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 9 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (6.2): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.39 over 168 reference and 93 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (6): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.39 over 168 reference and 93 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.37 over 188 reference and 129 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 31 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.38 over 36 reference and 2013 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 214 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.28 over 214 reference and 2013 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric.
The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric.

library.revisionNotes: Methodology 0.12 rebuild: reference stations selected by the fixed pressure screen, pools assembled per metric on the Level III to Level I ladder, and the five landscape pressure metrics scored on the fixed criteria of the Screening tier. No candidate inside this ecoregion passes the screen, so all 16 reference curves are borrowed from a comparable Level II or Level I pool under the comparability check, with the source geography and transfer risk recorded on each. Sixteen curves cover 16 of the 20 STAF functions. The four remaining functions carry a documented gap for insufficient reference support rather than a forced curve. The fast-water habitat curve is marked for verification against field data before it carries weight in a decision.

exclusions.justification: Every candidate metric for this function was withheld. The scored candidates are benthic total taxa richness and native fish taxa richness, and native non-tolerant fish taxa richness was also tested under Pre-registration III. Too few comparable least-disturbed stations carry them in this ecoregion or in its Level II and Level I parents. On comparable national donors the strongest result was native non-tolerant fish taxa richness on distance-matched donors, which reached promising: its class calls agreed with reference in 16 of 19 evaluation regions with no systematic promotion, but its recovered thresholds fell inside the true answer's uncertainty in only 9 of 19, against the 13 required to validate. No modeled expectation passed validation under the extrapolation this ecoregion requires. Ohio EPA's ecoregional biocriteria, the nearest applicable published criterion, were checked on 2026-09-21 and are not usable here on three independent grounds. They set thresholds on composite indices (the fish Index of Biotic Integrity, the Modified Index of well-being, and the Invertebrate Community Index) rather than on taxa richness, so applying one to a richness count would compare different quantities. Those indices are computed under Ohio EPA's own field protocol against metric lines calibrated on Ohio reference sites, and the NRSA archive carries no index column and cannot derive one. They are Ohio water quality standards keyed to a per-waterbody use designation, while 26 of this ecoregion's 51 stations lie in Indiana. No suitable basis was found among the sources evaluated, which is not a finding that this function cannot be scored. No curve was forced and the function is reported as unassessed, so the ecosystem condition index is stated as an interval.

A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 55), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 75 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 77.37 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region TPL, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests), 7 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.56 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.00, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 25 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 16 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 7 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (8.2): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (TPL): The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 53 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 105 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: A modeled specification for this metric passed the recovery test and waits for the owner's approval, so it is not used yet. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 83), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 8.1 (Mixed Wood Plains) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 52 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 8.1 (Mixed Wood Plains), 8 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.56 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.00, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 6 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 7 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (8.1): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.38 over 51 reference and 331 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.33 over 59 reference and 1014 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (NAP): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.38 over 113 reference and 253 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 53 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.40 over 129 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 91 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.34 over 91 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 16 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Measurement-precision floor. The Functioning core of this two-sided curve spans 0.268 Std. Units (7.96 to 8.23 Std. Units at n = 14), narrower than 0.4 Std. curveCaveats: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 8.1 (Mixed Wood Plains) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 40 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 8.1 (Mixed Wood Plains), none of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.56 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.00, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness
Allan 2004, Landscapes and riverscapes: the influence of land use on stream ecosystems
Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.
Agricultural bands are national screening tiers, not ecological criteria.
A result computed from one input is labeled partial.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 3 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 21 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 3 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 10 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 5 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 14 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 3 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 10 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Measurement-precision floor. The Functioning core of this two-sided curve spans 0.238 Std. Units (8.17 to 8.41 Std. Units at n = 17), narrower than 0.4 Std. Units, 2 times the metric's documented measurement precision of 0.2 Std. Units, so band assignments inside it would present measurement noise as condition classes and the metric is withheld at the build under rule CURVE-09. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 8 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level II pool (9.4): The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. The Level I pool (9): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.27 over 55 reference and 510 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (SPL): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.25 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 27 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.28 over 105 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 40 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.22 over 40 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 57), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 54 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 77.37 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region TPL, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests), 1 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.56 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.00, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

curveCaveats: pH carries natural geology (calcareous or naturally acidic waters) as well as disturbance, and a two-sided core narrower than measurement precision is noise rather than condition.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 42 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 77.37 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region TPL, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests), 1 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on base flow index, runoff, surficial lithology. The national scale analysis supports this metric at Level II, finer than the level borrowed from, so the transfer risk is moderate and the expectation may not represent local conditions.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 57), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 93 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 77.37 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region TPL, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests), 1 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, precipitation. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.61 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.14, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 25 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 17 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 1 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (8.2): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (TPL): The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. No other basis supports it either. criteriaSource.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

citations.text: USACE National Inventory of Dams

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.
metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 22 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 6 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 1 carries the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 4 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

curveCaveats: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference pool's lower quartile for this metric is at or below zero, so the curve is a three-point fallback rather than a fitted shape: the bands turn on very small differences and should be read as a coarse sort, not a measurement.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 37 least-disturbed stations from Level I 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests), 3 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. The national scale analysis supports this metric at Level III, finer than the level borrowed from, so the transfer risk is high and the expectation may not represent local conditions.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
metrics.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 3 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 19 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 4 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 13 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

metrics.howToMeasure: Bank height ratio (ratio) is scored on EASI's national screening method, Bank erosion and armoring, adopted because no other source supports this function here. Good ≤1.3, Fair >1.3-≤1.5, Poor >1.5.
metrics.methodContext: Bank height ratio at a representative riffle of the assessment reach: the height of the lower top of bank above the thalweg divided by the maximum bankfull depth (the stream quantification tools' field procedure, after Rosgen 2006). Measure it in the field; DEEP offers a DEM-derived value only where the cross sections pass the quality checks, and leaves the function unassessed until a value is entered.

curve.layerName: Adopted EASI screening method (provisional), Bank erosion and armoring

curveCaveats: An EASI screening method is a provisional national judgment that rates the quantity the same way in every region. It is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition, and its confidence is capped.

Rated on EASI's bank-instability bands for the bank height ratio (1.3 and 1.5), a provisional screening relationship rather than a measured erosion rate or an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition.
BHR does not detect existing armoring and does not directly measure erosion rate or eroding-bank extent.
The DEM-derived cross section is a susceptibility screen and may require surveyed geometry.
BHR is reused by floodplain engagement and channel adjustment and is therefore correlated evidence.

Candidate E5b (Addendum 2, 2026-09-28, owner decision D15): the rating is withheld where the 3DEP cross-section record is unreliable on its own terms (fewer than three sections carry the ratio, bankfull is extrapolated outside the Bieger fit range, every section found its bank by the crest scan, or the reach median bank-height ratio sits at the cap only with sections the DEM cannot resolve: bankfull depth at or below 0.15 m on a 10 m or 3 m model, 0.05 m on lidar) or the ratio is physically impossible (a bank-height ratio at or below 0, an entrenchment ratio below 1). A bank-height ratio at the floodprone cap on resolved sections reads at least 2, severe incision, and is rated. Geometry is otherwise a documented gap.

The state stream quantification tools rate channel and floodplain dynamics on the bank height ratio and on the share of eroding or armored bank, field measurements this archive does not carry. Where no station pool supports this metric the function is completed by measuring the bank height ratio at the assessment reach and scoring it on the published curve for the state (the Minnesota and Wisconsin tools, verified against their originals) or on the national Stream Functions Pyramid standard (1.0 to 1.2 functioning, above 1.5 not functioning), entered as a provisional source with its citation.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
metrics.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 19 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 18 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 2 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (12.1): 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level I pool (12): 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The NARS-9 pool (XER): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.45 over 50 reference and 99 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 6 matched national donors, below the floor of 10. 83 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.40 over 83 reference and 2037 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: Only 2 of this ecoregion's own streams carry the metric, fewer than the 10 a modeled reference needs to estimate the ecoregion's own level. metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 63), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Watershed wetland (%), woody plus herbaceous, both classes required; wetlands store surface water and attenuate flow peaks. EASI scores Surface water storage on the same sum (method watershed-wetland-extent).
metrics.methodContext: Percent of the watershed in woody plus herbaceous wetland (NLCD 2019). DEEP reads it from EPA StreamCat for the reach. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 63), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 24 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests), 10 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.56 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.00, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.
Scored on a reference pool whose transfer to this ecoregion was not confirmed by the recovery test (class agreement 0.56 of evaluation regions; two thirds required); confidence capped at 39.

metrics.methodContext: Road length per square kilometer of watershed. DEEP computes it for the delineated watershed. Nothing is measured in the field.

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Road-density proxy for concentrated inflow pressure

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
USDA Forest Service 2011, Watershed Condition Classification Technical Guide (FS-978)

limitations: Road density does not count actual outfalls or establish whether runoff is treated.
The 1 km/km² breakpoint is a screening judgment.

USFS watershed-condition guidance classes road density more strictly (good under 1, impaired over 2.4 miles per square mile, about 0.62 and 1.49 km/km²), derived from salmonid watersheds. EASI keeps the NRSA-anchored national screen and discloses the stricter alternative.

metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 63), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.
metrics.methodContext: Base flow index of the watershed, the percent of streamflow that comes from base flow (USGS base flow index grid). DEEP reads it from EPA StreamCat for the reach. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 63), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from NARS-9 region ecoregion CPL because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 23 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region CPL, 10 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.26 of 19 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.11, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 63), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Residual pool depth per 100 m; deeper residual pools generally better habitat.
metrics.methodContext: Measure the thalweg depth at 10 or 15 evenly spaced stations between each pair of transects (100 or 150 along the reach). The value is the mean residual pool depth in centimeters, computed from that depth profile and the reach slope with the NRSA physical habitat calculations.

metrics.howToMeasure: Bankfull width-to-depth ratio; both over-widened (very high) and incised (very low) degrade condition. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 23 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 2 carry the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 9 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (8.5): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.52 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The NARS-9 pool (CPL): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.42 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 32 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 25 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: A modeled specification for this metric passed the recovery test and waits for the owner's approval, so it is not used yet. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 20 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 5 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 1 carries the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 3 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). This ecoregion under the regional screen: The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level II pool (6.2): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 101 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 145 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 73), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 44 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests), 3 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.56 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.00, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness
Allan 2004, Landscapes and riverscapes: the influence of land use on stream ecosystems
Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.
Agricultural bands are national screening tiers, not ecological criteria.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 23 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 2 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 21 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 2 carry the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 13 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 10 (North American Deserts) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 106 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 10 (North American Deserts), 1 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.
Agricultural bands are national screening tiers, not ecological criteria.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 10 (North American Deserts) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 47 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 10 (North American Deserts), 1 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, air temperature. Every station drains to this ecoregion's faunal province. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.50 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.05, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (10.2): 2 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level I pool (10): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (XER): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 7 matched national donors, below the floor of 10. 68 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). metrics.sourceCitation: Adopted EASI screening method (provisional), Bank erosion and armoring
metrics.howToMeasure: Bank height ratio (ratio) is scored on EASI's national screening method, Bank erosion and armoring, adopted because no other source supports this function here. Good ≤1.3, Fair >1.3-≤1.5, Poor >1.5.
metrics.methodContext: Bank height ratio at a representative riffle of the assessment reach: the height of the lower top of bank above the thalweg divided by the maximum bankfull depth (the stream quantification tools' field procedure, after Rosgen 2006). Measure it in the field; DEEP offers a DEM-derived value only where the cross sections pass the quality checks, and leaves the function unassessed until a value is entered.

curve.layerName: Adopted EASI screening method (provisional), Bank erosion and armoring

curveCaveats: An EASI screening method is a provisional national judgment that rates the quantity the same way in every region. It is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition, and its confidence is capped.

Rated on EASI's bank-instability bands for the bank height ratio (1.3 and 1.5), a provisional screening relationship rather than a measured erosion rate or an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition.
BHR does not detect existing armoring and does not directly measure erosion rate or eroding-bank extent.
The DEM-derived cross section is a susceptibility screen and may require surveyed geometry.
BHR is reused by floodplain engagement and channel adjustment and is therefore correlated evidence.

Candidate E5b (Addendum 2, 2026-09-28, owner decision D15): the rating is withheld where the 3DEP cross-section record is unreliable on its own terms (fewer than three sections carry the ratio, bankfull is extrapolated outside the Bieger fit range, every section found its bank by the crest scan, or the reach median bank-height ratio sits at the cap only with sections the DEM cannot resolve: bankfull depth at or below 0.15 m on a 10 m or 3 m model, 0.05 m on lidar) or the ratio is physically impossible (a bank-height ratio at or below 0, an entrenchment ratio below 1). A bank-height ratio at the floodprone cap on resolved sections reads at least 2, severe incision, and is rated. Geometry is otherwise a documented gap.

criteriaSource.title: NRSA fish MMI condition benchmarks, NARS-9 region SPL

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Ecoregions Used in the National Aquatic Resource Surveys

limitations: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

The benchmarks rest on EPA's least-disturbed reference sites of 2008-09 and 2013-14 and their disturbance-adjusted 5th and 25th percentiles, a definition of reference that need not match this assessment's landscape-pressure screen; three regions had fewer than 30 such sites.

curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 9 (Great Plains) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 20 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 9 (Great Plains), 5 of them inside this ecoregion. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.50 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.05, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 6.2 (Western Cordillera) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 249 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 6.2 (Western Cordillera), 11 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.67 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.16, where at most 0.05 is allowed. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 8 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 8 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (6.2): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (6): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 35 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.27 over 39 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 80 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric.

No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.64 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.62 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level II pool (6.2): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.39 over 249 reference and 93 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (6): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.39 over 249 reference and 93 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.37 over 294 reference and 129 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 39 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.34 over 39 reference and 2013 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 397 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.29 over 397 reference and 2013 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13).
