metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 13 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 4 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 6 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 4 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 7 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.30 over 13 reference and 10 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). This ecoregion under the regional screen: The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.30 over 21 reference and 10 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level II pool (5.3): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.32 over 46 reference and 67 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (5): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.29 over 56 reference and 112 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (NAP): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.31 over 65 reference and 253 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 37 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.32 over 93 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 27 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.32 over 27 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. curveCaveats: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from NARS-9 region ecoregion UMW because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 100 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region UMW, 9 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.47 of 19 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.00, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from NARS-9 region ecoregion UMW because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 100 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region UMW, 9 of them inside this ecoregion. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 51), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from NARS-9 region ecoregion UMW because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 112 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region UMW, 9 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, precipitation. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.68 of 19 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.17, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 21 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 5 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 13 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 4 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 9 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (8.1): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (UMW): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 65 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 118 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: A modeled specification for this metric passed the recovery test and waits for the owner's approval, so it is not used yet. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 5 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 19 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 3 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 13 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 4 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.24 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level II pool (8.1): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.32 over 17 reference and 331 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.36 over 32 reference and 1014 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (NAP): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.36 over 31 reference and 253 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 42 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.40 over 318 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 13 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.22 over 13 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric.

Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
metrics.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 28 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 1 borrows comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 2 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.26 over 64 reference and 57 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). This ecoregion under the regional screen: The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.32 over 92 reference and 57 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level II pool (5.3): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.29 over 113 reference and 67 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (5): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.32 over 184 reference and 112 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (NAP): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.35 over 162 reference and 253 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 91 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.41 over 504 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 93 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.33 over 93 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 60), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: The reference expectation likely varies with ElevationClass (cross-validated improvement 28%, resample recurrence 100%); the curve is unstratified pending a larger reference pool, so sites at either end of that gradient may read as departures that are natural.
Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 8.1 (Mixed Wood Plains) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 43 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 8.1 (Mixed Wood Plains), 14 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.56 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.00, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 5 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 16 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 4 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 11 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 25 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 3 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 2 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.55 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 1.25 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level II pool (10.1): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.34 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level I pool (10): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (XER): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 73 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 204 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 1 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 6 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (9.2): 9 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level I pool (9): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.27 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The NARS-9 pool (TPL): 9 usable stations, below the floor of 10. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 32 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 30 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.32 over 30 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 5.2 (Mixed Wood Shield) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 100 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 5.2 (Mixed Wood Shield), 94 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 20 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 3 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 4 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 3 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 7 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.24 over 51 reference and 42 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). This ecoregion under the regional screen: The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.28 over 82 reference and 42 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level II pool (5.2): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.28 over 82 reference and 45 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (5): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.39 over 110 reference and 112 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (UMW): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.35 over 94 reference and 190 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 32 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.44 over 432 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 32 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.38 over 32 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness

Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
metrics.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 4 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 9 usable stations, below the floor of 10. curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 15), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 6.2 (Western Cordillera) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 264 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 6.2 (Western Cordillera), 32 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 25 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 1 curve is fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 3 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The Level I pool (6): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.41 over 287 reference and 93 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.39 over 339 reference and 129 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 100 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.33 over 135 reference and 2013 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 422 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.30 over 422 reference and 2013 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). curveCaveats: The reference expectation likely varies with ElevationClass (cross-validated improvement 26%, resample recurrence 100%); the curve is unstratified pending a larger reference pool, so sites at either end of that gradient may read as departures that are natural.
Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 9 (Great Plains) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 87 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 47.8 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region NPL, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 9 (Great Plains), 19 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
metrics.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 5 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 17 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 3 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 10 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Measurement-precision floor. The Functioning core of this two-sided curve spans 0.365 Std. Units (8.14 to 8.51 Std. Units at n = 56), narrower than 0.4 Std. Units, 2 times the metric's documented measurement precision of 0.2 Std. Units, so band assignments inside it would present measurement noise as condition classes and the metric is withheld at the build under rule CURVE-09. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 1 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.28 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level II pool (9.3): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (9): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (NPL): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). criteriaSource.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

citations.text: USACE National Inventory of Dams

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.
metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 17 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 7 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 5 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 1 carries the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 5 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Measurement-precision floor. The Functioning core of this two-sided curve spans 0.374 Std. Units (8.15 to 8.53 Std. Units at n = 25), narrower than 0.4 Std. Units, 2 times the metric's documented measurement precision of 0.2 Std. Units, so band assignments inside it would present measurement noise as condition classes and the metric is withheld at the build under rule CURVE-09. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.67 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.28 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level II pool (9.3): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (9): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 36), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 8.4 (Ozark/Ouachita-Appalachian Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 49 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 37.8 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region SAP, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 8.4 (Ozark/Ouachita-Appalachian Forests), 11 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 8 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.29 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The Level II pool (8.4): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.40 over 17 reference and 211 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (8): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.41 over 29 reference and 1116 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (SAP): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.37 over 25 reference and 344 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 11 matched national donors, but the donor pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.25 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. 6 national donors inside the comparability envelope, below the floor of 10. Modeled reference: The low-disturbance training streams cover the natural setting of 0% of this ecoregion's streams, less than the 7% of the weakest region the model was validated in, so the prediction would extrapolate past where it was tested. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include no regional criterion for turbidity. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 45), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: pH carries natural geology (calcareous or naturally acidic waters) as well as disturbance, and a two-sided core narrower than measurement precision is noise rather than condition.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 8.3 (Southeastern Usa Plains) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 71 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 37.8 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region SAP, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 8.3 (Southeastern Usa Plains), 25 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on base flow index, runoff, surficial lithology. The national scale analysis found this metric varies no more between Level III ecoregions than at the level borrowed from, so the transfer risk is low.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 15 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 11 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 15 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.56 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.00, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the exploratory floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (7.1): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.43 over 38 reference and 31 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (7): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.43 over 38 reference and 31 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.40 over 301 reference and 129 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 30 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.43 over 30 reference and 2013 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 520 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.32 over 520 reference and 2013 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 67), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 8.4 (Ozark/Ouachita-Appalachian Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 88 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 37.8 percent, the 90th percentile at EPA's NRSA reference sites in NARS-9 region SAP, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 8.4 (Ozark/Ouachita-Appalachian Forests), 34 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mapped dams within one mile is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good 0 mapped dams, Fair 1 mapped dam, Poor ≥2 mapped dams.
metrics.methodContext: Number of dams in the USACE National Inventory of Dams within one mile of the site. DEEP counts them. Note in the field any barrier the inventory does not show.

curve.layerName: EASI fixed criteria, Nearby dam-proximity proxy

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

citations.text: USACE National Inventory of Dams

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.
metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 9 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 7 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 8 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 4 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 4 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 6 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

metrics.howToMeasure: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 5), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 6.2 (Western Cordillera) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 150 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 6.2 (Western Cordillera), 12 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.

A result computed from one input is labeled partial.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.67 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.16, where at most 0.05 is allowed. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
metrics.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 2 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 15 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 3 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 10 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 9 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level II pool (6.2): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (6): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 55 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.26 over 84 reference and 1786 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 157 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document

Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams

No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level II ecoregion 10.1 (Cold Deserts) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 31 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 10.1 (Cold Deserts), 4 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 22 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 4 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 13 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 1 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (10.1): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (10): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.28 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The NARS-9 pool (XER): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 18 matched national donors, but the donor pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.49 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. 76 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

metrics.howToMeasure: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 81), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.16-provisional

curveCaveats: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 10 (North American Deserts) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 106 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 10 (North American Deserts), 2 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.44 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

curveCaveats: The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 10 (North American Deserts) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 104 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level I 10 (North American Deserts), 2 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, surficial lithology. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source promoted sites systematically. The test found class agreement 0.67 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.06, where at most 0.05 is allowed. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 20 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 16 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 1 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 2 usable stations, below the floor of 10. referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 5 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 10 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 10 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 4 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 4 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion.
